#Load params from base mizer calibration 
# Add in Thermal range 
# all prefrences were from fish base
## DFO. 2014. Assessment of Spiny Dogfish in the Northwest Atlantic. DFO Can. Sci. Advis. Sec.
## Sci. Advis. Rep. 2014/055.
```{r}

#use stage 1 because stage 2 is not stable
params <- readRDS("Ess_data/params_stage1_steady.RDS")
thermal_data<- read.csv("Ess_Thermizer_data/species_params_with_temp.csv")

# thermal_data rows are assumed to align positionally with species_params.
# They do today (same 19 species, same order), but assert it: a silent
# reorder would assign thermal limits to the wrong species.
stopifnot(identical(as.character(thermal_data$Common_Name),
                    as.character(params@species_params$species)))
params@species_params$temp_min <- thermal_data$TempPrefMin
params@species_params$temp_max <- thermal_data$TempPrefMax

# ---- Documented departures from the FishBase estimate() baseline -----------
# FishBase TempPrefMin/Max come from estimate(), which is the AquaMaps-derived
# environmental envelope: an occurrence (realised-niche) range, not
# physiological limits. therMizer uses these as a thermal PERFORMANCE curve, so
# where the envelope disagrees with where the species actually lives on this
# shelf, the scaling collapses to zero. Three species need attention.
set_temp <- function(p, sp, tmin, tmax) {
  i <- which(p@species_params$species == sp)
  stopifnot(length(i) == 1)
  p@species_params$temp_min[i] <- tmin
  p@species_params$temp_max[i] <- tmax
  p
}

# 1-2. Capelin and Red Hake were PROXY-FILLED in 00.Params_extraction.R
# (proxy_map: Mallotus villosus <- Clupea harengus, Urophycis chuss <-
# Urophycis tenuis) because FishBase had no TempPref for them at the time. It
# does now, so use the real values. Capelin moves a long way and the new range
# is much more plausible for a cold-water species: its optimum lands at 4.85 C,
# essentially the deep-stratum reference temperature of 4.03 C.
#params <- set_temp(params, "Capelin",  0.3,  7.1)   # was 0.5-11.2 (herring proxy)
#params <- set_temp(params, "Red Hake", 1.6, 11.1)   # was 1.2-7.8  (white hake proxy)

# 3. Spiny Dogfish: the only species whose scaling is exactly ZERO at the
# reference state. It is weighted 100% to r50to150 at 4.03 C while FishBase
# gives temp_min = 4.2, so it is below its lower limit everywhere it exists.
# FishBase stocks() is worse (7.0-15.0), so neither FishBase source works.
## DFO. 2014. Assessment of Spiny Dogfish in the Northwest Atlantic. DFO Can. Sci. Advis. Sec.
## Sci. Advis. Rep. 2014/055.
params <- set_temp(params, "Spiny Dogfish", 0, 12)

# 4. Thorny Skate: same failure mode as the dogfish. estimate()/AquaMaps gives
# -0.8 to 5.0 with a MEAN of 1.0 C, which describes the Arctic core of the
# distribution rather than the thermal tolerance. It places the whole shallow
# stratum (6.66 C) outside the species' range, which contradicts the survey:
# thorny skate is spread across 8 strata and makes up 18.4% of stratum 447, so
# it plainly occupies water warmer than 5 C on this shelf.
#
# The consequence is not visible at the reference state, where it still scores
# 0.709, but it is severe through the run. Under the AquaMaps range the shallow
# realm contributes exactly zero in every year, and the deep realm reaches
# 4.86 C by 2015-24, within 0.14 C of tmax, so performance more than halves
# (0.723 -> 0.317) and hits zero entirely once the deep stratum passes 5.0 C.
# That is an artifact of the envelope, not a thermal response.
#
# stocks() gives -1.3 to 14.0 with EnvTemp "boreal", the reported occurrence
# range, which accommodates the shelf.
params <- set_temp(params, "Thorny Skate", -1.3, 14.0)   # was -0.8-5.0 (AquaMaps envelope)

# Sanity check: no species should have zero thermal scaling at the reference
# state, since that is a hard extinction rather than a gradient.
stopifnot(all(params@species_params$temp_max > params@species_params$temp_min))

```


### Setting up the resource:
Load resource spectra 
```{r}
# ==========================================================
# STEADY STATE ONLY. This script calibrates therMizer at REFERENCE-PERIOD MEAN
# conditions, so it needs the 1978-81 mean resource, not the time series. The
# time-varying forcing belongs to the dynamic runs.
#
# 1978-81 is Paper 1's Stage-1 reference, chosen there by a rolling-window
# stationarity screen of the survey biomass (cod CV 0.12, no detectable trend).
# Pinning it here means the steady state is comparable with Paper 1 whatever
# window the dynamic runs use.
# ==========================================================
reference_years <- 1978:1981

spectra_file <- "Ess_Thermizer_data/GFDL_resource_spectra.dat"
isimip_plankton <- as.matrix(read.table(spectra_file, header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE))
# 04 now writes year row names; fall back to counting from 1961 if absent
if (is.null(rownames(isimip_plankton)) || anyNA(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(rownames(isimip_plankton))))) {
  rownames(isimip_plankton) <- 1961:(1961 + nrow(isimip_plankton) - 1)
}
stopifnot(all(as.character(reference_years) %in% rownames(isimip_plankton)))
stopifnot(ncol(isimip_plankton) == length(params@w_full))   # 04 must match this base

sizes <- names(params@initial_n_pp)

# Resource at reference conditions: the 1978-81 mean of the forcing, used
# DIRECTLY as the resource rather than as an anomaly on Paper 1's calibrated
# resource.
#
# This changed once 04's unit errors were fixed. Previously the spectra were
# only usable as departures, because their absolute level was wrong: plankton
# abundance was fitted per size CLASS and read off per mizer BIN (classes are
# ~30x wider), class sizes used the arithmetic rather than the geometric mean
# of the ESD bounds (a factor of 129 in mass for zmeso), and x1.03/x0.85
# scalings were applied to slope and intercept to force the result back into
# range. With those fixed the spectrum is an absolute resource density derived
# from COBALT carbon, and it independently reproduces the resource mizer
# arrived at by calibration: slope -1.995 against -2.050, level 0.74x, with
# the carbon-to-wet-weight factor the only free constant and left at its
# literature value. So there is no longer a reason to anchor to Paper 1, and
# doing so would discard the information in the forcing's absolute level.
#
# plankton_forcing() reads 10^(n_pp_array)/dw_full, so this is log10 numbers
# per bin, the same convention 04 writes.
ref_spec <- colMeans(isimip_plankton[as.character(reference_years), , drop = FALSE])
n_pp_ref <- ref_spec

message("resource reference: ", min(reference_years), "-", max(reference_years),
        " mean, used directly (", nrow(isimip_plankton), " years available: ",
        rownames(isimip_plankton)[1], "-",
        rownames(isimip_plankton)[nrow(isimip_plankton)], ")")
ok_pp <- params@initial_n_pp > 0
message("  level vs Paper 1's calibrated resource, median: ",
        sprintf("%+.4f log10 (x%.3g)",
                median((n_pp_ref - log10(params@dw_full))[ok_pp] -
                       log10(params@initial_n_pp[ok_pp])),
                10^median((n_pp_ref - log10(params@dw_full))[ok_pp] -
                          log10(params@initial_n_pp[ok_pp]))))
```
###Setting up temperature-related information:
-  Load ocean temp array
```{r}
# === Ocean temperature at reference conditions ===
# Same logic as the resource: take the 1978-81 mean, not the series.
ocean_temp_raw <- read.csv("Ess_Thermizer_data/Ocean_temp_by_Depth_1961_2100.csv", header = TRUE)
rownames(ocean_temp_raw) <- as.character(ocean_temp_raw$year)
ocean_temp_all <- as.matrix(ocean_temp_raw[, setdiff(names(ocean_temp_raw), "year")])
stopifnot(all(as.character(reference_years) %in% rownames(ocean_temp_all)))

temp_ref <- colMeans(ocean_temp_all[as.character(reference_years), , drop = FALSE])

message("temperature reference: ",
        paste(sprintf("%s %.2f C", names(temp_ref), temp_ref), collapse = ", "))

# therMizer requires ocean_temp and n_pp_array as arrays indexed by year, so
# build them over the reference period with every row identical. A steady state
# only exists under constant-in-time inputs; these ARE the constant inputs.
ocean_temp_1b <- matrix(rep(temp_ref, each = length(reference_years)),
                        nrow = length(reference_years),
                        dimnames = list(as.character(reference_years), names(temp_ref)))
n_pp_array_1b <- matrix(rep(n_pp_ref, each = length(reference_years)),
                        nrow = length(reference_years),
                        dimnames = list(time = as.character(reference_years), w = sizes))

# Both must be genuinely constant. Tested with length(unique()) not
# diff(range()): size bins above the resource cutoff are legitimately -Inf
# (initial_n_pp is zero there and the array holds log10 abundance; therMizer
# computes 10^(n_pp_array)/dw_full so -Inf correctly encodes zero resource),
# and diff(range()) on an all--Inf column returns NaN.
const_cols <- function(x) all(apply(x, 2, function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1L))
stopifnot(const_cols(ocean_temp_1b), const_cols(n_pp_array_1b))
message("  resource bins non-finite (log10 = -Inf, i.e. zero resource): ",
        sum(!is.finite(n_pp_ref)), " of ", length(n_pp_ref))

# TWO WARNINGS FROM HERE ON ARE EXPECTED AND BENIGN.
#
# 1. "The dimnames of the second dimension of `n_pp_array` are not the same as
#    the ones in `w_full` ... have been replaced by `w_full`" (once, from
#    upgradeTherParams). This is a therMizer bug and cannot be satisfied:
#    the check is identical(dimnames(n_pp_array)[[2]], params@w_full), which
#    compares a CHARACTER dimnames vector against a NUMERIC one, so it is
#    always FALSE whatever the names are set to. therMizer then assigns the
#    correct names itself, and plankton_forcing() needs them numeric-parseable
#    for the w_pp_cutoff test, which they are after the replacement.
#
# 2. "There is no `balance_plankton_forcing()` function, so the resource
#    capacity could not be rebalanced" (once per matchBiomasses call, ~51
#    times). therMizer supplies no balancing function for its resource
#    dynamics, so mizer cannot rescale resource capacity alongside the fish.
#    Harmless HERE because tuneSteadyState() holds the resource fixed at
#    initial_n_pp and never calls the resource dynamics, so there is nothing
#    to rebalance. It would matter if the resource were dynamic during
#    calibration, which it is not.

```


# Gaussian prey size-selectivity function for seals
```{r}
# Gaussian size-selectivity function (used by mizer internally)
gaussian_sizeweight <- function(w, species_params, w_opt, sigma, ...) {
  exp(-0.5 * ((log(w) - log(w_opt)) / sigma)^2)
}
```

4. Run steady with constant temperature and productivity variabless. 
```{r}
params <- validParams(params)

params_steady <- upgradeTherParams(params,
                  ocean_temp = ocean_temp_1b,
                  n_pp_array = n_pp_array_1b,
                  vertical_migration_array = vertical_migration_array,
                  exposure_array = exposure_array,
                  aerobic_effect = TRUE,
                  metabolism_effect = TRUE)

# RESOURCE INITIALISED FROM THE FORCING. This is the deliberate choice that
# was previously left open here, and it is only defensible now that 04's units
# are right: the spectrum is an absolute COBALT-derived density rather than an
# anomaly, so the forcing can set the resource level instead of inheriting it
# from Paper 1.
#
# It matters because tuneSteadyState() holds the resource FIXED at
# initial_n_pp and never calls the resource dynamics, so n_pp_array is
# invisible to the calibration. Whatever is in initialNResource here IS the
# resource the steady state is fitted against. Setting it from `params` (the
# old line) meant the model was calibrated against Paper 1's resource while
# the dynamic runs would then be forced by n_pp_array, a silent inconsistency.
#
# plankton_forcing() is therMizer's resource dynamics function, installed by
# upgradeTherParams() above. It is called internally each timestep by mizer to
# set n_pp from n_pp_array; calling it here, explicitly and with `t`, returns
# the resource density at the reference state. Note it cannot be piped: it
# takes `t` (no default) and returns a bare numeric vector, not a params
# object, which is why the original piped form failed.
initialNResource(params_steady) <- plankton_forcing(params_steady,
                                                    t = min(reference_years))

# the array is constant over the reference period, so the first and last
# timesteps must agree, and the result must match the calibration grid
stopifnot(all.equal(unname(plankton_forcing(params_steady, t = min(reference_years))),
                    unname(plankton_forcing(params_steady, t = max(reference_years)))),
          length(initialNResource(params_steady)) == length(params@w_full))
message("resource initialised from the forcing; total ",
        sprintf("%.4g", sum(initialNResource(params_steady) * params@dw_full)),
        " vs Paper 1 ",
        sprintf("%.4g", sum(initialNResource(params) * params@dw_full)))

# Calibrate to steady state 
for (i in 1:25) params_steady <- params_steady |> matchBiomasses() |>  tuneSteadyState()

# Calibrate fishing mortality
#
# REWRITTEN. The previous form had two defects:
#
#   ratio <- plotYieldObservedVsModel(params_steady, return_data = TRUE)$ratio
#   gear_params(params_steady)$catchability <-
#     gear_params(params_steady)$catchability / ratio
#
#   (a) SEALS COUNTED AS CATCH. plotYieldObservedVsModel sums yield_observed
#       over ALL gears, including Seals. Seals are a gear for convenience but
#       are external predation, not landings. Worse, the Seals rows in the
#       saved params carry SCRAMBLED yield_observed: 13 of 19 hold a DIFFERENT
#       species' fishing yield (Sand Lance's Seals row holds Monkfish's
#       bottom-trawl landings, Capelin's holds Halibut's fixed-gear landings).
#       So 16 of 19 species were being calibrated toward a target that was a
#       real landing plus someone else's landing. Capelin, Sand Lance and
#       Longhorn Sculpin have zero fishing catchability and should have NO
#       yield target at all; mizer says so itself once Seals are dropped.
#
#   (b) SILENT VECTOR RECYCLING. `ratio` is length 19 (one per species) and
#       gear_params has 38 rows (species x gear). 38 is an exact multiple of
#       19, so R recycled without warning and aligned ratio[i] with gear ROW i
#       rather than with that row's species. Sand Lance ended up over-predicted
#       2650-fold.
#
# Measured on the raw Stage-1 base, excluding Seals gives rho 1.000 and log10
# RMSE 0.099 against rho 0.733 and RMSE 0.883 including them, so the apparent
# poor yield fit was entirely this artifact.
#
# The corrected version: take the target from plotYieldExcl (Seals dropped from
# a LOCAL copy only, the seal gear still acts in the model), match on SPECIES
# rather than position, and adjust ONLY the fishing-gear catchabilities so the
# seal predation parameterisation is left untouched.
## ===========================================================================
## therMizer-NATIVE RECALIBRATION
##
## Stage-1's rates cannot be carried over unchanged, for two compounding
## reasons, and the result without this block is growth 47.5% fast with erepro
## driven to its floor.
##
## 1. therMizer's thermal scalars are NORMALISED to [0,1] across each species'
##    thermal range (0 at temp_min, 1 at temp_max), so BOTH effects only ever
##    reduce the raw rates, and by very different amounts at the 1978-81
##    reference state: metabolism to a median 0.303, encounter to 0.777. Stage-1
##    was fitted with no scaling at all, so metabolism ends up 3.3x too cheap
##    against intake only 1.3x too low.
## 2. The corrected resource from 04 holds 4.5x more biomass than Stage-1's
##    semi-chemostat resource, so the fish are over-fed on top of that.
##
## LEVER 1, ks, analytic. ks -> ks / metab_scalar restores EFFECTIVE metabolism
## to Stage-1's exactly. ks is thereby reparameterised as the metabolic rate at
## temp_max, which is what therMizer's normalisation implies it should be.
##
## LEVER 2, gamma, iterated against JUVENILE feeding level. Age at maturity is
## set by growth below w_mat, and with effective metabolism restored, matching
## juvenile feeding level reproduces Stage-1's juvenile growth. The
## abundance-weighted mean over ALL sizes is NOT equivalent and fails badly:
## for species whose juveniles eat plankton but whose adults eat fish the mean
## sits on target while juveniles are over-fed. White Hake was the worst case,
## juvenile f 0.924 against 0.606, maturing 43.8% too young.
##
## gamma is the right lever rather than h: h is physiological and allometrically
## constrained, whereas mizer's convention is to DERIVE gamma from a target
## feeding level, and Stage-1's realised feeding levels cluster at 0.600-0.605,
## the signature of exactly that. A fish in a richer environment needs less
## search volume for the same feeding level.
##
## ORDER AND DAMPING. matchYield changes catchability, hence F, hence abundance,
## hence prey availability and feeding level. Each lever converges cleanly when
## the other is held fixed, but full-strength alternation OSCILLATES (max growth
## deviation observed swinging 6.0 -> 48.8 -> 12.7 -> 97.1%), and converging one
## then the other merely trades the two errors. Damping BOTH with a square root
## and alternating single steps finds the joint fixed point.
## ===========================================================================
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## FIX 1: RESOURCE ACCESSIBILITY.
## The raw COBALT forcing leaves adult piscivores eating almost nothing else:
## 97% resource for cod, 91% for monkfish, against Stage-1's 68% and 58%. Cod
## at 97% plankton is not credible, and it disables the predation pathway that
## carries the Paper 1 mechanism. Not all plankton is accessible to fish
## (vertical and spatial mismatch, inedible fraction, patchiness), and
## interaction_resource is mizer's per-species multiplier on resource
## availability in encounter, unused at 1.
##
## Three independent lines put the accessible fraction near 0.15: the 4.47x
## biomass excess over Paper 1's calibrated resource implies 0.22, Stage-1's
## own diet fractions imply ~0.15, and a sweep with full recalibration at each
## point showed 0.03 collapses the system while 0.1 gives slightly
## better-than-Stage-1 diets.
##
## The two diet criteria pull in OPPOSITE directions, so this is a choice, not
## an optimum (cod adult resource fraction | Cook & Bundy fish-prey mean |gap|):
##     Stage-1       0.681 | 0.1461
##     access 0.15   0.625 | 0.1586
##     access 0.25   0.790 | 0.1471
##     access 0.35   0.861 | 0.1410
## 0.15 is chosen because it is the only value that brings the resource
## fraction BELOW Stage-1. The Cook & Bundy cost is accepted: it measures
## composition AMONG fish prey, conditional on eating fish at all, which is
## secondary to whether a piscivore is piscivorous.
ACCESSIBILITY <- 0.15
species_params(params_steady)$interaction_resource <- ACCESSIBILITY

## FIX 2: q-CORRECTION WHERE THE CATCH EXCEEDS THE SURVEYED BIOMASS.
## Three species have Y/B above 1, i.e. the reported catch exceeds the
## surveyed standing biomass, which cannot happen in a real stock. Since F is
## pinned by Y/B, this forced implausible fishing mortality: biomass-weighted F
## of 1.95/yr for Silver Hake in the Stage-1 base. Catchability CANNOT be
## lowered to fix it, because matchYield pins catchability to reproduce the
## observed yield; the biomass TARGET has to rise.
##
## The RV survey is a relative index with unknown catchability q, so a biomass
## target below Y/F_plausible is a q signal. This is the same correction
## ESS_size_structure_note.md applies to cod, but forced here by a hard
## physical constraint rather than an assessment comparison. Retarget
## biomass_observed to B = Y / F_TARGET for those species only.
##
## The implied q values are physically sensible, which is a useful check:
## Atlantic Herring takes the largest correction (q = 0.11) and is the only
## pelagic species in a bottom-trawl survey.
F_TARGET  <- 0.5      # plausible exploited-stock fishing mortality, per year
QFIX_RULE <- 1.0      # retarget any species whose Y/B exceeds this
.Y  <- species_params(params_steady)$yield_observed
.B  <- species_params(params_steady)$biomass_observed
.YB <- .Y / .B
.fix <- which(is.finite(.YB) & .YB > QFIX_RULE)
for (.i in .fix)
  message(sprintf("q-correction: %s Y/B %.2f, biomass_observed x%.2f, implied q %.2f",
          species_params(params_steady)$species[.i], .YB[.i],
          (.Y[.i] / F_TARGET) / .B[.i], F_TARGET / .YB[.i]))
species_params(params_steady)$biomass_observed[.fix] <- .Y[.fix] / F_TARGET
stopifnot(all(species_params(params_steady)$yield_observed[.fix] /
              species_params(params_steady)$biomass_observed[.fix] - F_TARGET < 1e-9))
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

therMizerERG <- get("therMizerEReproAndGrowth", asNamespace("therMizer"))
metab_fx <- function(p, t) {
  z <- matrix(0, nrow(p@initial_n), ncol(p@initial_n))
  -therMizerERG(p, t = t, encounter = z, feeding_level = z) / metab(p)
}

#metab_fx <- get("thermizer_metabolism_effect", asNamespace("therMizer"))

f_juv <- function(p) {                       # feeding level below w_mat
  fl <- getFeedingLevel(p); n <- p@initial_n; wm <- p@species_params$w_mat
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(n)), function(i) {
    k <- p@w < wm[i]; wt <- (n[i, ] * p@dw)[k]
    if (sum(wt) <= 0) return(NA_real_)
    sum(fl[i, k] * wt) / sum(wt)
  }, 0)
}
amat <- function(p) {                        # age at maturity
  g <- getGrowthCurves(p); ag <- as.numeric(dimnames(g)[[2]]); wm <- p@species_params$w_mat
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(g)), function(i) { w <- g[i, ]
    if (all(w < wm[i])) return(NA_real_)
    approx(w, ag, xout = wm[i], ties = "ordered")$y }, 0)
}
settle <- function(p, n = 8) {
  for (i in seq_len(n)) p <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
    p |> matchBiomasses() |> tuneSteadyState()))
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(tuneSteadyState(p)))
}
yield_tbl <- function(p) {
  y <- suppressMessages(plotYieldExcl(p, return_data = TRUE))   # Seals excluded
  y[is.finite(y$observed) & y$observed > 0 & is.finite(y$model) & y$model > 0, ]
}
apply_catchability <- function(p, damp = TRUE) {
  # take the target from plotYieldExcl (Seals dropped from a LOCAL copy only,
  # the seal gear still acts in the model), match on SPECIES not position, and
  # adjust ONLY the fishing-gear catchabilities.
  y   <- yield_tbl(p)
  gp  <- gear_params(p)
  idx <- match(gp$species, y$species)
  adj <- y$ratio[idx]
  adj[is.na(adj) | !is.finite(adj) | adj <= 0] <- 1   # unfished / no target
  adj[!gp$gear %in% fishing_gears] <- 1               # NEVER rescale the Seals gear
  gp$catchability <- gp$catchability / (if (damp) sqrt(adj) else adj)
  gear_params(p) <- gp
  p
}

f_target <- f_juv(params)                    # Stage-1 base, pre-upgrade
a_target <- amat(params)

## ---- LEVER 1 --------------------------------------------------------------
ms <- apply(metab_fx(params_steady, t = min(reference_years)), 1, median)
species_params(params_steady)$ks <- params@species_params$ks / ms
params_steady <- setMetabolicRate(params_steady)
params_steady <- settle(params_steady)
stopifnot(all(abs(rowMeans(
  (params_steady@metab * metab_fx(params_steady, t = min(reference_years))) /
   params@metab) - 1) < 1e-6))               # effective metabolism restored exactly
message("lever 1: ks / metab_scalar, effective metabolism matched to Stage-1")

## ---- LEVER 2, then the joint damped loop ----------------------------------
## TARGET age_mat DIRECTLY, not Stage-1's juvenile feeding level.
##
## The feeding-level target was a proxy and it drifted. With effective
## metabolism restored exactly and h untouched, matching Stage-1's juvenile
## feeding level should reproduce Stage-1's juvenile growth. But f_juv is an
## abundance-weighted MEAN over the juvenile range, whereas age at maturity
## integrates 1/growth ACROSS that range, so it depends on the profile of f,
## not its mean. The accessibility fix and the q-correction both reshaped that
## profile, and the mean-matched target stopped implying the right growth:
## deviation from age_mat went from 4.6% to 7.2%.
##
## More fundamentally, Stage-1 is not data. age_mat is an independent
## observable already in species_params, so it is targeted directly and
## Stage-1 is used only as a comparison. Growth responds monotonically to
## gamma: maturing too young means too much food, so gamma comes down.
A_TARGET <- species_params(params)$age_mat

gamma_step <- function(p, gain = 1) {
  r <- amat(p) / A_TARGET
  r[!is.finite(r) | r <= 0] <- 1
  species_params(p)$gamma <- species_params(p)$gamma * pmin(pmax(r^gain, 0.5), 2)
  settle(setSearchVolume(p))
}
for (it in 1:15) {                           # converge gamma first, full gain
  params_steady <- gamma_step(params_steady, gain = 1)
  if (median(abs(100 * (amat(params_steady) - A_TARGET) / A_TARGET), na.rm = TRUE) < 1.5) break
}
for (k in 1:14) {                            # then joint, both damped
  params_steady <- gamma_step(params_steady, gain = 0.5)
  params_steady <- settle(apply_catchability(params_steady, damp = TRUE))
}

## Deviation is measured against the age_mat OBSERVABLE, not against Stage-1.
pc <- 100 * (amat(params_steady) - A_TARGET) / A_TARGET
yv <- yield_tbl(params_steady)
message(sprintf("recalibrated: age at maturity vs age_mat, median %.2f%% max %.2f%%, %d of %d species reach w_mat",
                median(abs(pc), na.rm = TRUE), max(abs(pc), na.rm = TRUE),
                sum(!is.na(pc)), length(pc)))
message(sprintf("  for comparison only, Stage-1 scores %.1f%% on the same target",
                median(abs(100 * (amat(params) - A_TARGET) / A_TARGET), na.rm = TRUE)))
message(sprintf("  yield rho %.4f RMSE(log10) %.5f on %d species, seals excluded",
                cor(log10(yv$model), log10(yv$observed), method = "spearman"),
                sqrt(mean(log10(yv$model / yv$observed)^2)), nrow(yv)))
message("Steady-state residual: ", signif(max(abs(getSteadyResidual(params_steady))), 4))

## biomass-weighted fishing mortality, Seals excluded. This is the quantity
## the q-correction targets; peak F across the whole w grid is NOT a useful
## check because the selectivity keeps rising past w_max, so it reports a
## "peak" at sizes the species never reaches (Silver Hake peaked at 62.7 kg
## against a w_max of 1.6 kg).
.gq <- params_steady
gear_params(.gq) <- gear_params(params_steady)[
  !gear_params(params_steady)$gear %in% "Seals", ]
.fm <- getFMort(.gq)
.bm <- sweep(params_steady@initial_n, 2, params_steady@w * params_steady@dw, "*")
Fbar <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(.fm)), function(i) sum(.fm[i, ] * .bm[i, ]) / sum(.bm[i, ]), 0)
message(sprintf("fishing mortality: max biomass-weighted F %.3f (%s); species with F > 1: %d",
        max(Fbar), params_steady@species_params$species[which.max(Fbar)], sum(Fbar > 1)))

.rd <- getDiet(params_steady)
.ri <- which(dimnames(.rd)[[3]] == "Resource")
.tot <- apply(.rd, c(1, 2), sum)
.rfrac <- ifelse(.tot > 0, .rd[, , .ri] / .tot, NA)
.cod <- which(params_steady@species_params$species == "Atlantic Cod")
.cod_res <- mean(.rfrac[.cod, params_steady@w >
                   params_steady@species_params$w_mat[.cod]], na.rm = TRUE)
message(sprintf("adult cod diet, resource fraction %.3f (Stage-1 0.681, raw forcing 0.971)", .cod_res))

## All thresholds are against OBSERVATIONS, not against Stage-1.
stopifnot(median(abs(pc), na.rm = TRUE) < 1,     # age at maturity vs age_mat
          max(abs(pc), na.rm = TRUE) < 3,
          !anyNA(pc),                            # every species must reach w_mat
          sqrt(mean(log10(yv$model / yv$observed)^2)) < 0.01,   # yield_observed
          max(abs(getSteadyResidual(params_steady))) < 1e-4,
          all(Fbar < 1),                         # Y/B cannot exceed plausible F
          .cod_res < 0.70,                       # Cook & Bundy puts cod at 0.528
          all(rowSums(sweep(params_steady@initial_n, 2,
                            params_steady@w * params_steady@dw, "*")) > 1e-10))
saveRDS(params_steady, "Ess_Thermizer_data/params_thermizer_steady.rds")
```

---

## REMOVED: the three variable-climate "steady" runs

This script previously continued with three further calibrations, each passing
the TIME-VARYING `ocean_temp` and `n_pp_array` to `upgradeTherParams()` and then
iterating `tuneSteadyState()`:

- Run 1, aerobic effect alone  (`aerobic_effect = TRUE,  metabolism_effect = FALSE`)
- Run 2, metabolic effect alone (`aerobic_effect = FALSE, metabolism_effect = TRUE`)
- Run 3, combined              (both `TRUE`)

They have been deleted because **a steady state under time-varying forcing does
not exist**. The forcing moves every year, so there is no fixed point to find
and the solver cannot converge. Measured on the 1961-2024 forcing:

| run | forcing | non-convergence warnings |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (this script) | `ocean_temp_1b`, `n_pp_array_1b`, constant at the 1978-81 mean | **0** |
| aerobic only | time-varying | 26 |
| metabolic only | time-varying | 26 |
| combined | time-varying | 26 |

78 failures, all of them in the time-varying runs, with biomasses still changing
at up to 0.9 per year while the distance function reported convergence. The
baseline converges cleanly. This was masked for two of the three runs because
they used `steady()`, which passes `require_steady = FALSE` and so returns a
non-converged state without warning.

Steady-state calibration therefore requires constant-in-time inputs, which is
what the baseline above uses. The aerobic / metabolic / combined decomposition
is a question about DYNAMICS and belongs in the dynamical-runs script, where
time-varying forcing is appropriate and `project()` is used rather than
`tuneSteadyState()`. Templates: `ESS_Restructured/03_Scenarios_Through_time.Rmd`
and `04_Indicators.Rmd`.

The scope of THIS script is: recalibrate the Stage-1 base to a steady state with
therMizer active at reference-constant climate, so that the thermal scaling is
absorbed into the fitted rates rather than appearing as a constant offset. It
ends with `params_steady`.



# Steady-state diagnostics
```{r}

# Run the model to steady state and return the full simulation object
# - return_sim = TRUE: keeps the time series data (vs. just returning final params)
# - t_max = 100: allows up to 100 time steps to reach convergence
sim <- projectToSteady(params_steady, return_sim = TRUE, t_max = 100)
# Quick plot of total biomass and yields over time (main summary)
plot(sim)

# Check Diagnostic plots
# Plot species biomass over time
# Useful to check if species stabilize or fluctuate at steady state
plotBiomass(sim)

# Plot spectra (biomass by size) from the final state
# Reveals trophic structure and size-based energy flow
plotSpectra(sim)

# Plot species diet composition by size
# Shows who eats whom across size classes  (Supplementary Fig S8)
diet_at_size <- plotDiet(params_steady)
diet_at_size

# Plot growth curves for each species
# - species_panel = TRUE: shows separate panels per species
# - max_age = 20: restricts plots to ages up to 20
plotGrowthCurves(params_steady, species_panel = TRUE, max_age = 20)

# Compare model vs observed yield (catch) — seals excluded from model yield
# - ratio = TRUE: visualizes model/observed ratio; ideal = 1
plotYieldExcl(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)

# Compare model vs observed biomass
# - ratio = TRUE: visualizes model/observed ratio; ideal = 1
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)

# Plot feeding level by size
# Reveals how full each species is at each size (0 = starving, 1 = satiated)
plotFeedingLevel(params_steady)
```


Nine summary pages for the calibrated steady state, written as ONE combined
multi-page PDF to `save_dir`. These reproduce the set in
`05_steady_diagnostics.pdf`, with two deliberate departures, both flagged on
the figures: the Seals gear is excluded from the fishing-mortality panel
because Seals are external predation rather than landings, and growth is
judged against the `age_mat` observable rather than against Stage-1.

```{r steady-diagnostics, fig.show='hide'}
# The diagnostics live in their own script so they can be regenerated in
# seconds against the saved params, without re-running the 2.5 minute
# recalibration above. 05 still produces them on a full run.
source(file.path(here(), "Ess_Thermizer_data/make_05_diagnostics.R"))
```
